# Friday Dinner Fit for a Toronto Family of 4

For **CAD 120**, the best balance of **quick service, kid-friendliness, and dietary flexibility** is usually **Italian** first, then **Japanese** if you choose carefully. **Mexican** can work well for budget and customization, while **Thai** is the riskiest because spice can be harder to avoid across the menu.

## Toronto Dinner Comparison: Thai vs Italian vs Japanese vs Mexican

| Cuisine | Likely cost for 4 | Kid-friendliness | Dietary flexibility | Speed | Best fit |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Thai | CAD 90–130 | Medium | High for vegetarian, lower for spice-sensitive child | Fast to moderate | Good if you order mild dishes carefully |
| Italian | CAD 85–125 | High | High | Moderate to fast | Best overall for mixed family needs |
| Japanese | CAD 95–140 | Medium | Medium to high | Fast | Best if you keep it simple and avoid premium items |
| Mexican | CAD 80–125 | High | High | Fast | Strong budget choice if spice is controlled |

## Best Choice by Your Priorities

### 1) Italian
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Why it works:** easiest for a vegetarian adult and a spice-avoiding child.
- **Cost:** pasta, pizza, salad, and one shared appetizer can usually stay near budget.
- **Kid-friendly:** very high; most kids accept pizza, garlic bread, or plain pasta.
- **Order efficiently:** choose 1–2 large pizzas, 1 vegetarian pasta, 1 kid-safe pasta, and a salad to share.
- **Watch-outs:** drinks, add-ons, and delivery fees can push the total up quickly.

### 2) Japanese
- **Why it works:** very quick if you use sushi rolls, udon, or donburi.
- **Cost:** can fit budget, but specialty rolls and sashimi raise the bill fast.
- **Kid-friendly:** decent if you stick to tempura, plain rice, edamame, or mild noodles.
- **Order efficiently:** pick 2 rice/noodle bowls, 2 simple rolls, and 1 shared appetizer.
- **Watch-outs:** many menus include wasabi, spicy mayo, or fried items with extra cost.

### 3) Mexican
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/shop.svg
- **Why it works:** highly customizable and usually fast.
- **Cost:** often the best value if you choose tacos, burritos, or bowls.
- **Kid-friendly:** strong, as long as you avoid hot salsa and spicy fillings.
- **Order efficiently:** ask for mild seasoning, skip jalapeños, and build 4 simple items instead of combo platters.
- **Watch-outs:** some places lean spicy by default, so you need to specify mild.

### 4) Thai
- **Why it works:** good vegetarian options and solid value.
- **Cost:** often reasonable, but protein add-ons and multiple mains can creep toward budget limits.
- **Kid-friendly:** weakest fit because many dishes are naturally spicy or aromatic in ways kids may reject.
- **Order efficiently:** choose mild curries, tofu stir-fries, plain rice, and clearly request “not spicy.”
- **Watch-outs:** even mild Thai can still feel spicy to a child who dislikes heat.

## Fast Ordering Plan to Stay Under CAD 120

- **Best budget-safe order style:** 1 shared starter + 4 mains + water
- **Avoid:** soft drinks, desserts, extra proteins, premium rolls, and delivery fees
- **Ask for:** mild seasoning, sauces on the side, and one child-friendly plain option
- **Target spend:** keep food at **CAD 95–105** so tax and tip still stay near budget

## Quick Recommendation

- **Best overall:** **Italian**
- **Best value/customization:** **Mexican**
- **Best fast casual backup:** **Japanese**
- **Least suitable for your child’s spice preference:** **Thai**
